newsitem.title: CANADA: Canadian bonds close weaker amid drop in currency.
newsitem.headline: Canadian bonds close weaker amid drop in currency.

text.p: Canadian bonds closed weaker on Thursday, underperforming U.S. treasuries as a sharp drop in the value of the Canadian dollar to two-year lows and a softer U.S. bond market weighed on prices, analysts said.

"We're starting to see slightly more aggressive selling into the close," said Andrew Pyle, head of fixed-income research with ABN-AMRO Bank Canada. "It's the weakness in the Canadian dollar and if you look to the U.S. curve, things improved a little bit, but the tone is still weak."
Canada's 30-year benchmark bond fell C$0.40 to C$107.00 to yield 7.390 percent.
The U.S. 30-year bond fell 3/32 to yield 7.11 percent. The spread between the two widened to 28 basis points from 25 basis points at Wednesday's close.

Canadian and U.S. bonds began the session lower as investors looked ahead nervously to the release of Friday's U.S. economic data. The U.S. retail sales and producer price reports for March were expected to provided further clues about whether the U.S. Federal Reserve's Open Market Committee would hike rates again when it met in May.
But Canadian bonds were also hit by a drop in the Canadian dollar to a two-year low later in the session.
The Canadian dollar weakened after comments from a Bank of Canada official led to a selloff and intervention by the central bank.
Traders said the Bank of Canada bought Canadian dollars to support the currency when it hit a new two-year low at C$1.3945 (US$0.7171).

The currency eased after the central bank's Deputy Governor Tim Noel told Reuters in Lima, Peru that the Bank would not react to "every wiggle" in the currency, suggesting it had no plans to raise interest rates.

"A lot of players here in the domestic market are going to be factoring in a possible move up to the the C$1.40 level. If that's the case, then you're going to see the entire Canadian curve really underperform the U.S., regardless of what kind of data comes out tomorrow morning," said Pyle.
In other prices, the Government of Canada's 10-year benchmark bond fell C$0.30 to C$100.80 to yield 6.884 percent while the U.S. bond fell 2/32 to yield 6.91 percent.
The negative spread between the bonds narrowed to three basis points from six basis points at the close of trading on Wednesday.
The three-month cash T-bill yielded 3.17 percent against its U.S. equivalent which yielded 5.28 percent.
